subject: science
passage: In autumn, the leaves of many trees turn yellow and orange. This happens because chlorophyll, the green pigment that leaves use to capture sunlight, breaks down as the days grow shorter. Yellow and orange pigments that were in the leaf all summer, hidden by the green, then become visible.
passage_b: Not every autumn color was hiding in the leaf all along. The bright reds of many maples, for example, come from pigments called anthocyanins. Botanists have found that many trees begin producing these red pigments only in autumn, making them fresh just as the chlorophyll disappears.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the explanation of autumn leaf color in Text 1?

choices.A: By agreeing that all autumn colors are present in the leaf during summer
choices.B: By explaining why trees drop their leaves before winter
choices.C: By noting that some autumn colors come from pigments that are newly made
choices.D: By suggesting that red leaves capture more sunlight than green leaves

explanation.why: Text 1 says autumn colors appear because yellow and orange pigments that were "in the leaf all summer" are revealed. Text 2 begins, "Not every autumn color was hiding in the leaf all along," and explains that red pigments are made "only in autumn." So Text 2 adds that some colors are newly produced.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 says the opposite: "Not every autumn color was hiding in the leaf all along."
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 never discusses why or when trees drop their leaves.
explanation.C: Correct. Text 2 explains that red anthocyanins are produced fresh in autumn rather than revealed, which adds to Text 1's explanation.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 does not compare how much sunlight red and green leaves capture.
